Scale: 1,067 sessions · 53,362 attributed contributions (47,290 spoken in the chamber, 6,072 submitted in writing) · 2,473 identified persons · 76 years of proceedings Why this chamber is different The Bundesrat is not a second elected chamber. Its members are delegates of the sixteen Land governments, appointed and recallable by them. Article 51(3) of the Basic Law requires each Land to cast its votes einheitlich as a bloc and the chamber has no Fraktionen (no party affiliations).
There is therefore no party field, and its absence is a design decision rather than a gap: the operative political unit is territorial. Every contribution carries the Bundesland it was made for, which makes territorial representation and federal–state conflict directly measurable from text. The chamber is also permanent, never dissolved, no elections, continuous session numbering since 1949 so the corpus is a single unbroken series rather than one segmented by legislative period.
Dataset files speeches.parquet, one row per attributed contribution by a named member: speaker name, resolved person_id, role, Bundesland, full German text, and contribution_type marking whether it was spoken in the chamber or submitted to the record in writing (102 MB). Gender is not stored here; join persons.parquet on person_id. persons.parquet, one row per resolved individual: canonical name, all name variants merged, career span, modal role and Bundesland, gender. # The Bundesrat corpus: A dataset of political discourse in the German Federal Council
## 1 Background & Summary
To address the aforementioned data gap, in this Data Descriptor, we present a complete speaker-attributed corpus of 1,067 Bundesrat plenary sessions from the chamber’s first sitting on 7 September 1949 to 10 July 2026. It comprises 53,362 speeches delivered in the chamber including written statements.
## 2 Methods
### 2.2 Data Source
It is published in different period-based web pages (e.g., 1949–1950, 1951–1955, …, 2026–2030) as PDF documents. Each PDF document represents one session and the filename carries useful information, including session number and date that are essential for building the metadata. The corpus is designed to be extensible; thus, newer sessions can be added accordingly.
## 3 Data Records
### 3.1 Dataset Overview
The dataset contains four tables built from 1,067 per session attribution files and the extraction catalog by a packaging step that performs no parsing of its own. Every field in the corpus is either carried from the attribution files or computed by aggregation so the package can be built at any time without disturbing the speech layer.
All text fields are UTF-8 encoded, null values are represented as null in Parquet and as empty strings in the CSV file. The dataset is publicly available on Zenodo https://zenodo.org/records/22086439 under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY4.0).

The data were collected in the research project "Political cohesion under conditions of fiscal scarcity - German federalism in the time of COVID-19" (funded by VolkswagenStiftung). The first dataset, labeled as "CovDebate", encompasses a total of 3,117 parliamentary proceedings related to Covid-19 that were debated in the German Bundestag and the 16 state parliaments between 1 February 2020 and 26 September 2021. The dataset includes the titles of the proceedings and contextual variables that facilitate a detailed analysis. The second dataset, labeled as "CovFed", comprises 4,610 manually coded statements of political parties that were identified in a qualitative content analysis of 212 key parliamentary debates in the same investigation period. The statements reflect different discursive strategies parties employ in the federal arena. The dataset covers all parties represented in the Bundestag as well as the "Freie Wähler"; all parliaments at both levels of government (Bundestag and 16 state parliaments); and three Covid-19-waves. It contains the statements as well as contextual variables, enabling a detailed analysis of the data. The new dataset is a novel and unique contribution to federalism scholarship because it provides insights into political behavior in the federal arena. It also contains analytical categories which are relevant beyond the German case and in political contexts other than Covid-19

# The Bundesrat corpus: A dataset of political discourse in the German Federal Council
## 1 Background & Summary
To address the aforementioned data gap, in this Data Descriptor, we present a complete speaker-attributed corpus of 1,067 Bundesrat plenary sessions from the chamber’s first sitting on 7 September 1949 to 10 July 2026. It comprises 53,362 speeches delivered in the chamber including written statements.
## 2 Methods
### 2.2 Data Source
It is published in different period-based web pages (e.g., 1949–1950, 1951–1955, …, 2026–2030) as PDF documents. Each PDF document represents one session and the filename carries useful information, including session number and date that are essential for building the metadata. The corpus is designed to be extensible; thus, newer sessions can be added accordingly.
## 3 Data Records
### 3.1 Dataset Overview
The dataset contains four tables built from 1,067 per session attribution files and the extraction catalog by a packaging step that performs no parsing of its own. Every field in the corpus is either carried from the attribution files or computed by aggregation so the package can be built at any time without disturbing the speech layer.
All text fields are UTF-8 encoded, null values are represented as null in Parquet and as empty strings in the CSV file. The dataset is publicly available on Zenodo https://zenodo.org/records/22086439 under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY4.0).

corpus-agent.snippet: The Bundesrat is Germany's second legislative chamber and a constitutional veto player within its political system. The members of the Bundesrat are delegates of state governments. Tracing the political discourse in the Bundesrat is challenging as it has a limited machine-readable corpus available. To address this issue, we present a speaker-attributed corpus of 1,067 Bundesrat plenary sessions from the chamber's first session on 7 September 1949 to 10 July 2026. In this period, a total of 53,362 speeches by 2,473 individuals were delivered in the chamber, including written statements. Each speech includes a speech ID, the full German text, the speaker's name, the date and location of the session, the federal state that the speaker represents, the speaker's role (if applicable), the type of contribution, and the speaker's gender. The dataset provides interdisciplinary research opportunities across computational political science, legislative studies, and parliamentary discourse analysis, coupled with discourse from the Bundestag.
